title: Locale-sensitive score calibration and latency-aware fallback chain for cross-encoder rerankers
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Improve cross-encoder reranker selection and rollouts by introducing per-locale score calibration plus a latency-aware fallback chain that preserves quality while meeting p95 latency SLOs. Background: Cross-encoder variants we currently maintain produce differently scaled scores across languages and model families, which complicates hybrid routing and A/B experiments. In high-latency situations or capacity pressure we should fallback to lightweight alternatives without degrading rank quality below an agreed threshold. This ticket will: 1) define and validate calibration approaches (temperature scaling, isotonic regression, Platt scaling) per locale and per-model; 2) implement a normalization layer in the rerank API that maps raw model logits to a common score space; 3) add routing logic to prefer lower-latency model variants under load while ensuring quality regressions are below guardrails; 4) add automated regression checks and per-locale smoke tests into the CI pipeline. Out of scope: retraining base cross-encoders or changing underlying tokenization. Success criteria: - MAP@10 improvement or parity compared to current baseline for >= 80% of locales after calibration. - End-to-end p95 latency with fallback enabled must not exceed current SLO by more than 10% under typical traffic. - Automated regression suite catches any quality regressions > 2% absolute on monitored test sets per locale. - Rollout can be toggled per-customer and per-region via console rollout configuration.
tasks: Design per-locale calibration experiments and select top-2 methods (Ava)
Create calibration dataset: 10k queries per major locale, stratified by query length (PM)
Implement normalization layer in rerank API (ENG)
Add latency-aware policy in smart router (ENG)
Instrument metrics: per-locale MAP@10, p50/p95 latency, throughput and model cost
Build regression CI jobs and add to nightly run
Run canary across 5% traffic in dedicated region, collect 72h metrics
Document fallback playbook and rollback thresholds
acceptance_criteria: Per-locale calibration models selected and evaluated (results uploaded to confluence)
Normalization layer integrated and tested against synthetic score distributions
Smart router falls back to lightweight reranker when estimated impact < defined quality loss
Nightly regression suite signals failures with a clear ticket creation path
Canary rollout shows no more than 2% drop in MAP@10 and p95 latency within 10% of baseline
comments: 2026-02-20 Ava Martinez: Created ticket after spike showed inconsistent score scales between xenc-small and xenc-large in es, fr, ja. Proposed per-locale isotonic vs temperature scaling experiment. Filed initial dataset generation task.

2026-02-28 Liam Chen: Completed dataset curation for EN/ES/FR/JA (10k queries each). Preliminary isotonic results: small reduction in MAP variance but overfits on low-data locales. Temperature scaling gave more stable gains. Recommendation: run both and compare over validation folds.

2026-03-05 Research note (Liam): Ran batch of 48 experiments. Temperature scaling + mean-variance normalization produced consistent score alignment across model families; MAP delta vs baseline: EN +0.6%, ES +0.8%, FR +0.3%, JA -0.1% (noise). Added experiment artifacts to dashboard. Next: integrate normalization layer for live canary.

2026-03-08 Engineering update (Nina Patel): Implemented normalization middleware in rerank API (feature branch). Middleware supports per-model, per-locale calibration tables and a lightweight on-CPU fallback path. Filed PR #1423 for review.

2026-03-10 PM review (Rafael Ortiz): Reviewed rollout plan. Agreed on canary at 5% in europe region, rollback if MAP@10 drops >2.0% or p95 increases >20%. Also requested an explicit cost delta estimate for using larger cross-encoder variants in canary.

2026-03-12 QA (Sofia Lee): Added nightly regression tests. First run flagged a 2.6% MAP drop for JA when normalization applied to xenc-legacy; assigned follow-up to investigate locale data sparsity and recalibration with isotonic. Action: reduce JA canary to 1% until addressed.
